FIXUP: FROMLIST: ASoC: SOF: Add Sound Open Firmware driver core If CONFIG_SND_SOC_SOF=y and CONFIG_SND_SOC_SOF_NOCODEC=m, builds fail with ld: sound/soc/sof/core.o: in function `sof_machine_check': >> sound/soc/sof/core.c:269: undefined reference to `sof_nocodec_setup' ld: sound/soc/sof/sof-acpi-dev.o: in function `sof_acpi_probe': >> sound/soc/sof/sof-acpi-dev.c:220: undefined reference to `sof_nocodec_setup' This happens because sof_nocodec_setup() is called from code built into the kernel but resides in a module. Since sof_nocodec_setup() is called unconditionally from the SOF core, SND_SOC_SOF_NOCODEC must be enabled if SND_SOC_SOF is enabled. This means that SND_SOC_SOF_OPTIONS must be enabled as well. Change-Id: I4e87b999970b1f630dd8e5ddddcc9162ab9b50ea Reported-by: kbuild test robot <lkp@intel.com> Signed-off-by: Guenter Roeck <groeck@chromium.org> Reviewed-on: https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/1662077 Legacy-Commit-Queue: Commit Bot <commit-bot@chromium.org> Reviewed-by: Curtis Malainey <cujomalainey@chromium.org>

Reland "glibc: use __builtin_constant_p to skip trivial FORITFY checks" This is a reland of e2847859919eff7358e22e3c25e7059bfc24613a, which was reverted due to http://crbug.com/971440 . Now that the fix has landed (I3bc82e876c03a371820815ba4d0c64e8abee55ca), we can try to reland this. Original change's description: > glibc: use __builtin_constant_p to skip trivial FORITFY checks > > This is only done on functions which are presumed to be hot and > often-used, and which are trivially optimizeable by the compiler. > > The hope is that this might both make CrOS faster, and make the cost of > things like automatic initialization less: the compiler can't exactly > reason about arbitrary _chk functions, but it has a much easier time > reasoning about a regular memcpy, for example. > > BUG=None > TEST=Tryjobs > > Change-Id: Iae794f4e129abe262e7381b419202a490a9de9f7 > Reviewed-on: https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/1638320 > Commit-Ready: ChromeOS CL Exonerator Bot <chromiumos-cl-exonerator@appspot.gserviceaccount.com> > Tested-by: George Burgess <gbiv@chromium.org> > Legacy-Commit-Queue: Commit Bot <commit-bot@chromium.org> > Reviewed-by: Manoj Gupta <manojgupta@chromium.org> BUG=chromium:971440 TEST=glmark2 passes with I3bc82e876c03a371820815ba4d0c64e8abee55ca applied Change-Id: Iede906d62ef5c982a7cd682317c7d3eb52c8f469 Reviewed-on: https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/1656730 Tested-by: George Burgess <gbiv@chromium.org> Commit-Ready: George Burgess <gbiv@chromium.org> Legacy-Commit-Queue: Commit Bot <commit-bot@chromium.org> Reviewed-by: Manoj Gupta <manojgupta@chromium.org>

FROMLIST: shellcheck: Add support for shflags Upstream PR at https://github.com/koalaman/shellcheck/pull/1604. This adds a new --uses-shflags option to shellcheck that makes it recognize DEFINE_string et al. as variable creation sites. Now shellcheck will not claim that the resulting FLAGS_nnn variables are referenced without assignment. As a bonus, it will also warn about command-line arguments that are defined and never referenced. BUG=chromium:898564 TEST=shellcheck --uses-shflags src/scripts/build_image Change-Id: I6498a1ebb732e2eb39b4c32da9a1683a9f51d9e9 Reviewed-on: https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/1649069 Tested-by: Benjamin Gordon <bmgordon@chromium.org> Commit-Ready: Benjamin Gordon <bmgordon@chromium.org> Legacy-Commit-Queue: Commit Bot <commit-bot@chromium.org> Reviewed-by: Chris McDonald <cjmcdonald@chromium.org>

CHROMIUM: iwl7000: mvm: check for length correctness in iwl_mvm_create_skb() We don't check for the validity of the lengths in the packet received from the firmware. If the MPDU length received in the rx descriptor is too short to contain the header length and the crypt length together, we may end up trying to copy a negative number of bytes (headlen - hdrlen < 0) which will underflow and cause us to try to copy a huge amount of data. This causes oopses such as this one: BUG: unable to handle kernel paging request at ffff896be2970000 PGD 5e201067 P4D 5e201067 PUD 5e205067 PMD 16110d063 PTE 8000000162970161 Oops: 0003 [#1] PREEMPT SMP NOPTI CPU: 2 PID: 1824 Comm: irq/134-iwlwifi Not tainted 4.19.33-04308-geea41cf4930f #1 Hardware name: [...] RIP: 0010:memcpy_erms+0x6/0x10 Code: 90 90 90 90 eb 1e 0f 1f 00 48 89 f8 48 89 d1 48 c1 e9 03 83 e2 07 f3 48 a5 89 d1 f3 a4 c3 66 0f 1f 44 00 00 48 89 f8 48 89 d1 <f3> a4 c3 0f 1f 80 00 00 00 00 48 89 f8 48 83 fa 20 72 7e 40 38 fe RSP: 0018:ffffa4630196fc60 EFLAGS: 00010287 RAX: ffff896be2924618 RBX: ffff896bc8ecc600 RCX: 00000000fffb4610 RDX: 00000000fffffff8 RSI: ffff896a835e2a38 RDI: ffff896be2970000 RBP: ffffa4630196fd30 R08: ffff896bc8ecc600 R09: ffff896a83597000 R10: ffff896bd6998400 R11: 000000000200407f R12: ffff896a83597050 R13: 00000000fffffff8 R14: 0000000000000010 R15: ffff896a83597038 FS: 0000000000000000(0000) GS:ffff896be8280000(0000) knlGS:0000000000000000 CS: 0010 DS: 0000 ES: 0000 CR0: 0000000080050033 CR2: ffff896be2970000 CR3: 000000005dc12002 CR4: 00000000003606e0 DR0: 0000000000000000 DR1: 0000000000000000 DR2: 0000000000000000 DR3: 0000000000000000 DR6: 00000000fffe0ff0 DR7: 0000000000000400 Call Trace: iwl_mvm_rx_mpdu_mq+0xb51/0x121b [iwlmvm] iwl_pcie_rx_handle+0x58c/0xa89 [iwlwifi] iwl_pcie_irq_rx_msix_handler+0xd9/0x12a [iwlwifi] irq_thread_fn+0x24/0x49 irq_thread+0xb0/0x122 kthread+0x138/0x140 ret_from_fork+0x1f/0x40 Fix that by checking the lengths for correctness and trigger a warning to show that we have received wrong data.
